steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease one 9 or 10 inch tube pan.
Combine the sugar, flour, salt, cinnamon, soda, oil. With an electric mixer beat in the eggs one at a time. Stir in the carrots and the walnuts. Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 1 hour 20 minutes. Note: this cake can be made in two 9 inch layer cake pans just change the baking time to 40 minutes.
To Make Frosting: With an electric mixer blend the cream cheese and cream. Add the vanilla and confectioners' sugar. Frosting can be spread and a still warm cake.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Carrot Cake
raw_recipe.description: This recipe makes a fabulous and moist carrot cake. Try it for Thanksgiving instead of or in addition to pumpkin pie.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Carrot Cake

review.reviewBody: After taking a while to review all of the carrot cake recipes on this site and others, I finally decided on this one but made a few adjustments that made the cake come out absolutely perfect. I would give the one I ended up making 5+ stars, but since I had to change this recipe a little I only gave this recipe a 4. Anyway, to change it, I added 1 tsp of baking powder in addition to the 1 tsp baking soda (so many other recipes called for both). I cut down the oil to 1 cup and it was still wonderfully moist. I used a 1-pound bag of carrots to grate and it was roughly the 3 cups that was suggested and I omitted the walnuts (I don't care for nuts in cakes as they take away from the moist texture, in my opinion). I baked it in two 9-inch round pans at 325 in my convection oven for only 35 minutes and they came out perfect. If using convection I wouldn't go any more than 35 minutes before checking it. And I used the cream cheese frosting II recipe on this website vs. the one in this recipe because I thought that it was way too much sugar as opposed to cream cheese. One more thing that I think made mine really yummy-- I used Pampered Chef's Korintje Cinnamon spice for the 2 tsp cinnamon and it gave it such a true cinnamon taste. Edited 10 years later: This, with the above modifications, is still my favorite and most-requested cake to make. I make it every year for Easter and birthday's and it's everyone's favorite. Great in cupcake form, too!

This is an excellent carrot cake! Dense, moist, and flavorful. Hubby raved about it 'til the end. I reduced the oil by 1/2 a cup, added 1/2 cup of natural applesauce, and omitted the walnuts, as neither of us like them. I used my Ninja to make the carrot really small (personal preference) instead of just grating. I opted to cook in a 9x13 pan at 340 for an hour. Next time I might add more cinnamon, but that's mostly because I like cinnamon and also to play with recipes, lol.

The frosting is another story. I made the recipe version and quickly realized I'd just made a yummy glaze (probably great on a bundt/tube cake), but not a frosting, so I started over with the Cream Cheese II Frosting (minus 1 cup sugar), which was much better, especially when storing the whole thing in the 'fridge, which is how we like carrot cake.

I followed this recipe as written and reduce it by half to make cupcakes. The only confusing part is the ounces written for the cream cheese. A package of cream cheese is 8 ounces not 3. So I went with my gut and used 4 ounces for my half recipe. This yield 9 cup cakes. I baked them for 40 mins. The cake was moist and texture ratio was perfect. The frosting was easy and turned out silky and smooth. Very delicious!!! My son approved. Thank you

Simple recipe that turned out delicious! Read the reviews befor I made this and I took the advice from others by reducing the oil to 1 cup and used 1 tsp of baking powder in addition to the baking soda. Since I made these changes I rated it a 4/5 because according to others it is not a 5/5 as is. Still saving this one in he books to make again with these positive changes. I made my own cream cheese frosting, not the frosting from this particular recipe. I used two 9 inch pans baking them at 325 for 35-40 minutes.

I thought 1 1/2 cups of oil would be too much, but the recipe came out delicious. I used Bertolli olive oil, extra light taste. I did add 1/2 tsp nutmeg and 1 tsp vanilla. Baked 2 rounds at 350 for 40 minutes, came out perfect. Easy baking is just what this busy mom needed.

I will make this again - great way to use a lot of carrots. I made the recipe almost as is; I used more carrots than called for, to get rid of what I had, but it didn't change the flavor. If anything, the cake was very moist and had a perfect consistency. I made in 2 8" cake pans, and put the left-over batter in mini-muffin tins. This cake was so good I ended up not putting any frosting on it, we ate it plain and it was delicious!

This is my second time making this and it is always a huge hit. I did use a full 8 ounces of cream cheese with the 2.5 cups of confectioners sugar because I felt the icing was too sweet otherwise. I also made this with gluten free flour due to the fact that I have an allergy. Turned out perfectly with the GF flour! Tried and true recipe!

I made it but took the recommendations of others and only used 1 cup of oil but then changed it to 1/2 c browned butter and 1/2 c oil. I baked it in 2 9" pans for 35 minutes and frosted it with Cream Cheese Frosting II from All Recipes. It was perfection!

I made this carrot cake. It's very moist and tasty. I did make a few changes by substituting the flour for cake flour, only using 1 cup of vegetable oil and using 3- 9 inch cake pans. Baking the 3 cakes at 350° for 25 minutes. My husband loves it.

I use unsweetened applesauce for most of the oil. I also add coarsely chopped walnuts and shredded coconut to the batter. What a wonderful treat!!!! Canned, drained, crushed pineapple might be a yummy addition too. I'm sure you wouldn't want to put more than 1/4 c. In the batter.
Amazing. I cut the oil to one cup, as others had recommended, and use a cup of honey instead of two cups of sugar. Perfect.
Love it
Its more sugar than I would ever use but it was delicious 😋
I used Coconut oil that is the only change I made.
All I can say is, "yummy, yummy, yummy!!" Lisa Kingston, ON

This was a quick easy recipe, and the first Carrot cake I've ever made. The first time I made it as suggested, everyone loved it, I thought it was too oily. The second time I cut the oil to one cup and it came out perfect. For the frosting I used 2 packages of cream cheese and enough powdered sugar to get it to my level of desired sweetness (maybe a cup?).
Easy and yummy
Super easy and delicious
My grandson loved this cake I made for his birthday. Carrot cake is his favorite. I made it according to the directions and it was excellent n

Made this recipe as directed except I used 2 tsp of baking soda. Put it in a 9 inch bundt pan and the family thought it was terrific. I think it raised up perfect, heavy and moist but not too heavy. My frosting looked pretty sloppy but that was operator error, texture and taste were good.
